annotations.text:
Storage first, then resume, then create.
Creating a session on landing would orphan one already in progress — so the app looks in localStorage, calls GET /sessions/:id, and only then POSTs a new one.

The graded demo.
Answering Yes reveals both questions in place and announces them; answering No removes them and the page converges. Pruning is watched, not hidden two screens back — which is the whole case for one page over a wizard.

Server-rejected submit.
A summary that is reachable, not just visible, focus moved to the first invalid item, and messages built from codes — the body never echoes an answer.

Respondent scale: 52px option rows, 44px inputs, 16px type — deliberately larger than the shared 32px primitives, which stay as they are in admin.
No painted status bar: the real one draws on top.

Open question 1 — list controls.
One filter box, a status segment, one sort menu. Column headers are not sort affordances, so the order on screen is never ambiguous. Default matches the server's id DESC; the rest is client-side over the whole list.

Open question 3 — where publish validation lands.
A rail fed by POST /draft/validate, running the identical code publish runs, keyed to item numbers with the offending rows marked. The editor cannot show green where publish would say no.

Open question 4 (frontend doc §10) — how visible the 409 path is.
Proposed: reorder is optimistic and snaps back with a toast; the banner is the only thing that stops the author, and it offers exactly one action.

Editing a question from inside the draft re-pins that item to the new version — the gesture is unambiguous. Every other questionnaire keeps the version it pinned.
Option ids never change, which is what makes the v2 relabel safe.

Open question 2 — which control renders each type.
Five types, one control each, plus the Yes/No template and the freeform Other behaviour. Only the date control was pinned before this.
Open question 5 — the editor's constraint fields per type, with the six cross-field rules made unrepresentable rather than reported.

Open question 4 — how errorsByItemId is built from an RFC 9457 body, for both apps.
One gap found: the ten draft codes have no message catalogue yet.
